questions.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1}
$$

Given that $C$ has the LU factorization $C=LU,$ then $L=$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U.
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that
$K=[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 7 & 3\end{aligned}]$
has the LU decomposition $K=LU,$ then $L=$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $K$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $K$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}K & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & 0 \\ 7 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 7 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{7}{4}){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{7}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot K \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -7 & -1 \\ 0 & 7 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot K \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -7 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}K=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}K & =U \\ {E}_{1}K & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ K & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ K & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -\frac{7}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ K & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{7}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ K & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ \frac{7}{4} & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}4 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -7 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & -5 & 9 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices.

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & -5 & 9 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{2}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -6 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} & ⟺ & \,\overset{{E}_{3}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot {E}_{2}\cdot {E}_{1}\cdot A \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{3},$ ${E}_{2},$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ {E}_{2}{E}_{1}A & ={E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ {E}_{1}A & ={E}_{2}^{-1}{E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}{E}_{3}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{32}=-2,$ ${u}_{33}=3,$ and ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{33}=-6.$
